subject.title: fix(plugins): detect orphan diagnostics with explicit code marker (2-part fix)

question: Should legacy no-code/no-pluginId persisted diagnostics be invalidated in the runtime snapshot loader, or should that cleanup move to a migration/doctor path while runtime only trusts explicit orphan markers?
rationale: The PR fixes a real stale-startup path, but the legacy fallback is a compatibility choice that partially reintroduces the no-pluginId inference previously rejected by maintainers.

options.title: Runtime explicit markers only
options.body: Remove or sharply narrow the legacy fallback so runtime stale detection trusts `orphan-source-path` plus missing source, and handle older rows through a separate migration/doctor path.

options.title: Approve a narrow legacy matcher
options.body: Keep runtime legacy cleanup only if it can identify old missing-load-path diagnostics without catching generic no-pluginId diagnostics, with tests and live upgrade proof.

options.title: Accept broad legacy rederive
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept rederiving for all no-code/no-pluginId missing-source diagnostics, but that waives the current guardrail against perpetual rediscovery.

recommendation.title: Runtime explicit markers only
recommendation.body: Remove or sharply narrow the legacy fallback so runtime stale detection trusts `orphan-source-path` plus missing source, and handle older rows through a separate migration/doctor path.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent gave the prior explicit-marker direction and is the clearest owner for deciding whether this PR still matches that boundary.
